title: CSM Skills Suite — Adversarially Validated Findings: Execution, Intent-vs-Function Gaps, and Improvement Priorities

tldr.content: Adversarial validation of the first review changed the picture: 3 of 8 original findings were materially overstated (plan-closure was grandfathered by design; producer drift was mostly misattributed; the trace count was understated), 5 held, and independent challengers plus a completeness sweep found ~27 additional verified defects, several more severe than the originals. The single most serious new defect is a broken security control: the tier-2 sandbox's required credentialsNone attestation always reads true because parseInspect reads Docker's non-existent HostConfig.Env (verified on real Docker). Next: an allowlist bypass via double URL-encoding (proven), a bootstrap-payload drift gate that ignores metadata-mapped runtime modules (reproduced, and neither pre-commit nor CI runs the check that would catch it), ungated corpus JSON (including a tracked 256-error .agents/builds record), and a cluster of SKILL-vs-code contract contradictions (csm-scan paths, csm-review corroboration/E1 fields, csm-review-python severity, csm-upload receipt, csm-bdd-tdd package, csm-deep-research states/marker) that make documented behavior fail validation or produce nothing. The Jev finding is upheld and strengthened: the provider violates two live schema requirements (missing state and missing instructions), so advice is null on every default path and one bad question poisons a whole batch.

executiveSummary.content:
Method (DEEP, hybrid): a first synthesis was attacked by two independent challenger agents (explicit instruction to falsify), then re-verified by two independent verifier agents and one exhaustive completeness sweep; the highest-severity new claims were reproduced by hand (real docker inspect, live Jev probes, egress evaluateEgress, ajv over the corpus, csm-ddd CLI runs). Roles stayed separated: challengers did not author findings, verifiers re-derived counts and re-ran code.

Shape:
  first review -> adversarial challenge x2 -> independent verify x2 + completeness sweep -> hand repro of top claims -> validated set

Outcome: original findings 5 upheld (2 strengthened), 3 downgraded/retracted; ~27 new validated defects, led by one broken security control (docker credentialsNone), one allowlist bypass (egress double-encoding), one packaging gate blind spot (payload metadata), one ungated corpus with real invalid records, and a long tail of SKILL-vs-code contradictions and doc drift.

Caveats: still a small number of independent agents (2 challengers, 2 verifiers, 1 sweeper); Docker egress controls were reviewed statically plus one live inspect, not a full live egress exploit; Jev rankings are advisory and non-authoritative.

keyFindings.content:
Severity: CRITICAL/HIGH first.
K1. supported — Docker sandbox credentialsNone is always true (reads HostConfig.Env; Config.Env holds the env). Required control dead; test enshrines the bug. [ref-docker][ref-autodocker]
K2. supported — egress pathPrefix allowlist bypass via double URL-encoding (%252e%252e). Proven. [ref-egress]
K3. supported — payload-drift gate ignores mapping.metadata; runtime modules under payload/lib/** can drift unchecked by check-suite/CI. Reproduced. [ref-checksuite][ref-pack][ref-regen]
K4. supported — corpus gating covers only plans + csm-build-state; .agents/builds holds a tracked 256-error record, research has 5 invalid + 14 unregistered-id records, reviews 2 invalid; only legacy .md is gated. [ref-corpus][ref-builds]
K5. supported — Jev live path violates two required fields; 12/25 points lack instructions AND state:null is rejected, so even valid points fail by default, and one bad question 400s the whole batch. [ref-openrouter][ref-points][ref-endpoint]
K6. supported — egress audit row dropped on allowed-forward error and relay swallows it -> worker hangs unaudited. [ref-egress]
K7. supported — unbounded relay/wrapper buffers; maxBytes not enforced on responses; relay binds 0.0.0.0 unauthenticated. [ref-egress][ref-sandbox]
K8. supported — bypass route skips the run lease and reuses dirty worktrees. [ref-driver][ref-executor]
K9. supported — csm-review binding receipt unwired -> VERIFIED with zero receipt; docs claim three-layer gate. [ref-loopclosure][ref-enfmodel]
K10. supported — SKILL-vs-code contradictions: csm-scan norms path, csm-upload receipt, csm-bdd-tdd package, csm-review-python severity, csm-review corroboration bump/E1 redacted, csm-deep-research states/marker, csm-plan review /1-only. [ref-scanskill][ref-reviewskill][ref-reviewvalid][ref-pyskill][ref-bddskill][ref-uploadskill][ref-planresolver][ref-drskill]
K11. supported — evaluator receipts are deterministic self-attestation (forgeable at receipt layer) but the guard recomputes work, so no closure bypass; csm-build requires the receipt only for /2. [ref-loopeval][ref-buildstate]
K12. supported — 9 source schemas unregistered (6 used in production/ad-hoc), compatibility matrix missing pairs (negotiate throws, latent), config-inventory and enforcement-evaluator-spike docs stale, bootstrap trust root is the test fixture, node24 canary non-blocking. [ref-registry][ref-matrix][ref-configinv][ref-enfspike][ref-bootstrap][ref-ci]

detailSections.content:
D1 Security (K1,K2,K6,K7): the docker-worker-provider credentialsNone control is the most serious new finding — a required attestation that can never fail (reproduced on real Docker). The egress broker's pathPrefix check is bypassable by double-encoding (reproduced); its audit ledger drops allowed-but-thrown forwards and the relay swallows the error (worker hangs unaudited); its buffers and the wrapped Docker/HTTP outputs are unbounded and post-forward maxBytes is unenforced; the relay binds 0.0.0.0 without auth. Recommend treating these as the first remediation tranche.
D2 Evidence substrate (K4,K5,K12): the corpus gate is narrower than the corpus — .agents/builds (256-error tracked record), research (5 invalid, 14 unregistered ids incl. 5 using the nonexistent csm-deep-research/1), reviews (2 invalid), approaches/decisions are ungated; docs/config-inventory falsely states builds is validated. Jev is doubly broken live (state + instructions), the failure is silent by design, and no gate or telemetry surfaces it.
D3 Contracts and drift (K3,K10,K11): SKILL bodies contradict the shipped code in at least seven skills, so following the SKILL yields schema-invalid records or nothing at all (csm-scan path, csm-review redacted/adjudicate, csm-review-python severity, csm-upload receipt, csm-bdd-tdd package, csm-deep-research states/marker, csm-plan /2 review). The payload-drift gate and the producer/registry surfaces leave these invisible.
D4 Enforcement honesty (K11): the 'independent evaluator' is deterministic self-attestation; csm-review's receipt is unwired; csm-build's receipt is /2-only while the default is /1; make precommit is not a CI mirror. The docs disclose some of this; the net is that the deterministic loop guard, not the evaluator, is the only real enforcement — worth stating plainly in the docs.
D5 Long tail: csm-ddd relative --repo and --help broken plus an undocumented cross-skill import contradicting its isolation claim; csm-grill writer has no mkdir and no caller; csm-autoresearch live-mode guard unreachable; bootstrap trust root is the test-fixture keyring presented as signature-verified; docs/config-inventory and enforcement-evaluator-spike stale; Makefile .PHONY omissions; csm-browse port unit tests non-hermetic.

recommendation.content:
Decision-ready priority order. Pilot readiness: none of these authorize production use of tier-2 isolation until K1/K2/K6/K7 are fixed.

1. Fix the credentialsNone control (K1): read entry.Config.Env; correct the fixture; add a test that feeds a real container with -e SECRET and asserts credentialsNone=false. Highest severity, small change.
2. Harden egress (K2,K6,K7): reject residual %2e/%5c after a fixed-point decode; write a ledger row on every decision including errors; respond and audit on malformed/malformed-forward; cap relay/wrapper/response buffers and enforce post-forward maxBytes; default the relay to loopback unless a policy opens it.
3. Close the payload-drift blind spot (K3): include mapping.metadata in buildPayloadSrcMap or run regen verifyFresh in the hook and CI. Verify: mutate a lib/render-html file and confirm the gate fails.
4. Gate the whole corpus (K4): add .agents/builds, research, reviews, approaches, decisions to validate-corpus-v2 (or a new validator); repair the 256-error builds record; register or explicitly mark-local the 14 unregistered research ids; fix docs/config-inventory.
5. Fix the Jev provider contract (K5): always send a non-empty instructions per question and a non-null state; reject at construction any point without instructions; add an opt-in live parity test (key-gated) plus a schema-shape assertion.
6. Reconcile SKILLs with code (K10): csm-scan norms path, csm-review redacted/E1 and corroboration bump, csm-review-python severity enum (or map C/R/W/E/F/Nit to the enum), csm-upload receipt (implement or downgrade the claim), csm-bdd-tdd package (wire createBddPackage into the pipeline or drop the product claim), csm-deep-research states/marker, csm-plan review /2.
7. State enforcement honestly (K11): document that the deterministic guard, not the evaluator, carries enforcement; either wire csm-review's receipt or remove the claim; decide whether /1 builds need the receipt.
8. Bypass safety (K8) and registry/docs hygiene (K12): acquire the lease on the bypass path and reset/reject dirty worktrees; register the 6 production schemas; add the missing compatibility pairs; replace the test-fixture trust root in the packaged bin or hard-fail non-production_use; fix doc counts and the named script.

What would change the recommendation: if tier-2 isolation is never exercised on untrusted code, K1's real-world impact is reduced (but the control is still wrong); if egress is never exposed beyond loopback, K2/K7 lower. Cost of being wrong on K1/K2 is a security control that cannot detect leakage; on K4/K5 it is silent loss of advice and unverified durable evidence.

unverifiedClaims.content:
- K2 (egress double-encoding) is proven at the policy-evaluation layer; end-to-end exploitability depends on the upstream decoding the forwarded path a second time. Verification: run a broker against a controlled double-decoding upstream.
- K7's memory-DoS requires a compromised or malicious worker/upstream; not demonstrated end-to-end, only by code inspection of the unbounded paths.
- The credentialsNone impact is bounded because the provider create path passes no -e flags today; exposure requires an image-embedded secret or a future env-injection change. Verification: inspect the created container with a deliberately insecure image.
- Whether some unregistered schema ids (.agents/docs, .agents/evidence, bootstrap) are intentionally local is undisclosed; verification: read the relevant plans/registries.
- Jev rankings and this review's severity assignment are single-analyst opinions with independent-agent confirmation; they carry no gate authority.

processAppendix.content:
Tier DEEP, mode hybrid. Tracks: (1) trace/execution, (2) plans/corpus, (3) prior findings vs HEAD, (4) skill-vs-tool/packaging, (5) runtime/security, (6) gates/tests, (7) schemas/registry.
Adversarial round 1 (challengers, anti-anchored, instructed to falsify): 2 agents attacked the 8 original findings; 3 were downgraded/retracted, 5 upheld (2 strengthened). Round 2 (independent verifiers): 2 agents re-derived counts and re-ran code on the new findings; a third agent swept for anything missed. Hand repros by the primary: real docker inspect (credentialsNone), live Jev probes (state/instructions/batch), evaluateEgress double-encoding, ajv on .agents/builds (256 errors), csm-ddd CLI (--help exit 2).
Gates run: check-suite OK (14 skills, 1169 checks); payload drift 374 compared/0 issues (does not cover metadata); validate-corpus-v2 94 records/0 failures (does not cover builds/research/reviews); regen verifyFresh ok at HEAD (fails on metadata mutation).
Jev advisory (live 2026-09-26, typesafe/jev-1.13, advisory only): ranked the candidate defects; no confidence returned for noul.
Control journal: INTAKE; TRIAGE DEEP/hybrid; RESEARCH 7 tracks; SYNTHESIZE; CHALLENGE round 1; VERIFY round 2 + hand repro; SAVED.
Limitations: 2 challengers + 2 verifiers + 1 sweeper; live egress exploit not run end-to-end; Jev and severity assignments are non-authoritative.

claims.statement: UPHELD, STRENGTHENED (was '12/25 inert'). Live: the provider omits BOTH required fields. Every question needs a non-empty instructions; every request needs a non-null state. The adapter sends state: input.state ?? null (openrouter.mjs), and decideBatch/consultPoints default state=null, so even the 13 instruction-bearing points return null unless a caller supplies state. Additionally one instruction-less question poisons an entire batch (mixed good+bad -> HTTP 400, all null). Verified live 2026-09-26: state omitted -> 400; state null -> 400; state string + instructions -> 200; mixed batch -> 400. The shipped offline tests assert the request shape against a mock, so none of this is caught.

UPHELD. No gate validates live provider behavior: all decision tests inject fetchImpl mocks; the required adapter suite (scripts/adapter-required-tests.mjs) lists browse/autoresearch/outcome-parity, not Jev. Fail-open is absolute (transport.send never throws) AND silent (adapter .stats() has no consumer; persistAdapterDecisions writes nothing unless a decision was applied; the advisory verdict is guarded by if(verdict) so null emits no trace). A live 400 ships green and invisible.

RETRACTED AS A DEFECT / corrected. The 9 complete plans with 30 open tasks are all pre-2026-09-14 and explicitly grandfathered by scripts/validate-plan-lineage.mjs (PLAN_LINEAGE_CUTOFF), which fails any post-cutoff complete plan retaining non-terminal tasks or blockers; running it yields 0 findings. The '37/72 complete plans lack completionReview' figure conflated populations: only 7 of 42 complete plans have a null completionReview, and completionReview is required-but-nullable, so null is schema-valid. Post-cutoff closure is gate-enforced. (Related real issue: the ~40 ungated/invalid corpus JSON records in claim-n-corpus.)

UPHELD in conclusion, corrected count. trace.jsonl spans 3 active days (2026-09-20..26, 4-day silence) and tracing was introduced 2026-09-20, so it cannot evidence a 3-week history; the durable 3-week+ record is .agents/plans (back to 2026-08-03) and git. Correction: fixture dominance is ~531/559 (the prior '401/559' was the whole 2026-09-26 day total, of which 378 were fixtures), i.e. the problem is worse than stated. The parallel .agents/evidence/orchestrator/*.jsonl (2312 files, 2026-09-05..26) is also harness fixture output, not production history.

UPHELD. bootstrap/package/payload/skills/csm-browse ships lib/, schemas/, SKILL.md only; the mirrored SKILL.md is byte-identical to source and references scripts/browse.mjs (17 refs); pack-bootstrap maps csm-browse lib+schemas; payload-index records the runtime closure as excluded. The exclusion is a recorded decision, but the shipped guidance ('One-time setup: pnpm install; node scripts/check-skill.mjs') is impossible from the payload.

DOWNGRADED. Real: csm-review/producer.json pins csm-review-findings/1 while SKILL.md:320 calls /2 'the current revision' (the /2 path is rejected by csm-plan — see claim-n-review-input). Non-defects: schemas/registry.json having no 'producers' key is by design (it is a schema registry; all producer schemas are registered); the scan canonicalPath 'NORMS.json' is CORRECT and SKILL-enforced-by-test, so the outlier is csm-scan/SKILL.md (claim-n-scan-path); missing 'format' headers on research/norms producers are cosmetic (no schema/test asserts the header).

UPHELD (counts) / DOWNGRADED (framing). 23 hardcoded $HOME/.config/opencode/skills paths remain in csm-browse (16), csm-upload (6), csm-deep-research (1); packaged copies identical. They are correct for the canonical opencode install but non-portable (bootstrap/protocol.md makes the destination agent-chosen), and for packaged csm-browse they point at unshipped scripts. The earlier 'csm-orchestrate SKILL omits a runtime AGENTS.md mandates' is overstated: SKILL.md:41 names the orchestrate() entrypoint; the driver/worker seam is only 0 refs, a low doc-consistency gap.

UHOLLD (verified on real Docker). parseInspect reads entry.HostConfig.Env, which Docker never sets; container env lives at entry.Config.Env. So inspect.env is always [] and the REQUIRED attestation control credentialsNone (docker-worker-policy.json) is always true. Reproduced: a container started with -e CSM_SECRET_MARKER=leaked parsed to env=[] while Config.Env contained the secret. The sibling csm-autoresearch provider reads Config.Env correctly. The test fixture enshrines the bug (tests/orchestrate-docker-worker-provider.test.mjs:298-303 puts Env inside HostConfig) and decision-gate injects a synthetic top-level env, so no test catches it.

UPHELD (proven). egress-broker pathPrefix matching decodes once then posix.normalize; /allowed/%252e%252e/admin decodes to /allowed/%2e%2e/admin, survives normalize, and passes an /allowed prefix. Reproduced: /allowed/ok allowed, /allowed/%2e%2e/admin denied, /allowed/%252e%252e/admin ALLOWED. Against an upstream that decodes again this escapes the path allowlist. High for allowlist fidelity.

UPHELD. On an allowed upstream forward that throws (non-timeout), the catch rethrows before activeBroker.record(), so no egress.decision row is written; the relay path swallows via .catch(()=>undefined), so the worker gets no response and hangs until its timeout. Violates 'one authoritative ledger row per decision'.

citations.locator: throw before record; swallow in relay

claims.statement: UPHELD. The relay buffer (buffer += chunk) is unbounded (newline-delimited only), connections[] is unbounded, Docker stdout/stderr capture and HTTP forward bodies are unbounded, and the matched rule maxBytes is enforced pre-forward only, never on the response. A compromised worker or malicious upstream can OOM the host. The relay also binds 0.0.0.0 with no auth.

UPHELD. Provision-time drop-capture degradation fails closed when required, but mid-run collectDrops only returns a degraded flag that verified-sandbox-runtime discards; requireDropCapture is not re-checked, contradicting docs/dynamic-worker-runtime.md ('fails closed only when the policy requires it'). Silent loss of a mandatory audit signal.

UPHELD. realModeBypass (--plan/--request) never acquires the run lease (only realMode does, and it returns before), writes a shared .agents/evidence/orchestrator/<runId>/bypass-result.json (last writer wins), and agent-session-executor reuses any existing worktree without a cleanliness/run binding, so concurrent or repeated bypass runs can collide or build on stale uncommitted state.

DOWNGRADED. Receipts are deterministic self-attestation: createEvaluatorReceipt derives the verdict from the same record and self-signs receiptDigest=digest(body); verifyEvaluatorReceipt only checks self-consistency, so a forged receipt verifies at the receipt layer, and closePlan accepts receipt ?? latestEvaluatorReceipt without comparing input digests. HOWEVER closePlan/loop-guard independently recompute outstandingWork and re-lint acceptance signals, so a fabricated receipt cannot close a record with real work remaining. Real finding: the receipts are not independent authorities and docs/enforcement-model.md's 'independent evaluator' is a harness/prose claim; not a closure bypass.

UPHELD. csm-review's binding-receipt layer is prose-only: assertCanSaveVerified/createEvaluatorReceipt in loop-closure.mjs have no production caller, the findings schema has no receipt field, and the production guard never requires one. docs/enforcement-model.md claims a VERIFIED save requires a complete receipt + guard + canSaveVerified; only two exist, so a VERIFIED record with zero receipt passes.

UPHELD (disclosed). csm-build requires the evaluator receipt only for csm-build-state/2; the production writer defaults to /1, so default-path builds reach COMPLETE with only the deterministic guard. Disclosed in docs/enforcement-model.md and scoped in state.mjs; lower severity, but the default path lacks the advertised receipt.

UPHELD (partially disclosed). make precommit runs fmt+regen+check-suite+lint+11 test files; make test fans out to 22 targets and CI additionally runs make check/test-corpus/test-package-index/etc. docs/enforcement-model.md's 'a cycle that lands green locally lands green in CI' is an overclaim (the subset nature is disclosed). No CI job runs regen, so metadata payload drift is invisible (claim-n-payload-metadata).

UPHELD (reproduced). check-suite buildPayloadSrcMap iterates only manifest.skills and mapping.supportingFiles, never mapping.metadata, and the drift walk is scoped to payload/skills; pack-bootstrap maps real runtime trees (payload/lib/**, payload/schemas/**) as metadata. Reproduced: appending to lib/render-html/index.mjs left check-suite green, while regen verifyFresh reported payload/lib/render-html/index.mjs mismatch. Neither the pre-commit hook nor CI runs regen/precommit, so a runtime-module drift can ship in the bootstrap package. The gap is disclosed in a code comment but unguarded.

UPHELD. 9 source schemas declare csm-*/N $ids but are absent from schemas/registry.json; 6 are exercised by production/ad-hoc validators (child-attempt, skill-executor, autoresearch-docker-attestation/policy, final-receipt) and 3 are deliberately unregistered per tests (trace, skill-manifest, verification-status). csm-orchestrate/lib/contracts.mjs hand-loads 29 schema files bypassing the registry, so these get no immutable-revision/digest/compat guarantees.

UPHELD. schemas/compatibility-matrix.json has no entries for csm-orchestrate-adversarial-review 1->2 or final-review 1->2 (and lacks same-revision pairs for many multi-revision bases such as cursor 2->2, capabilities 1->3/3->3); the compatibility runtime throws 'unregistered compatibility pair'. Production asserts /2 directly, so no live path fires today, and no test enumerates registry vs matrix.

UHOLLD.
